icd10_codes.description: Sprain of ligaments of cervical spine, initial encounter
Laceration without foreign body of scalp, initial encounter
Jumping or diving into swimming pool striking bottom causing other injury, initial encounter
Swimming pool (public) as the place of occurrence of the external cause

dialogue:
[doctor] hi , {PATIENT_FIRST} ? i'm doctor {DOCTOR_LAST} , i'm the emergency physician today . i know you've got that collar on , so please do n't try to turn your head . just look at me and answer with words .
[patient] okay . hi .
[doctor] so the paramedics told me a little bit , but tell me in your own words what happened .
[patient] so we were at the {CITY} community pool for my nephew's graduation party . and i was swimming with the kids , and i got out and i dove off the side , and i did n't realize i was at the shallow end . it was only like four feet deep .
[doctor] okay .
[patient] and i went in head first and my head hit the bottom of the pool . like the top of my head scraped right along the concrete .
[doctor] okay . did you lose consciousness at all ?
[patient] no , i do n't think so . i kind of saw white for a second , but i came right up . my buddy {OTHER_FIRST} grabbed me and the lifeguard came over , and they saw i was bleeding from my head .
[doctor] okay . did you swallow a lot of water ? any trouble breathing ?
[patient] no , i swallowed a little , but i'm breathing fine .
[doctor] okay . and after you hit , did you have any numbness , tingling , or weakness in your arms or legs ? even for a second ?
[patient] no . my neck hurt right away , and my head was bleeding , but my arms and legs felt normal the whole time .
[doctor] okay , good . any electric shock feelings going down your arms ?
[patient] no .
[doctor] okay . the lifeguard put you on a backboard and called the ambulance ?
[patient] yeah , they did the whole thing , the board and the collar .
[doctor] okay , that's exactly what they should do . so where does your neck hurt ?
[patient] in the back , in the middle , and kind of down into my shoulders . it's stiff .
[doctor] okay . on a scale of one to ten ?
[patient] maybe a five .
[doctor] okay . any headache ?
[patient] a little bit , where i cut it .
[doctor] any nausea or vomiting ? any vision changes ?
[patient] no .
[doctor] have you had any alcohol today ?
[patient] i had one beer , like two hours before .
[doctor] okay . any medical problems ? any medicines ?
[patient] no , nothing .
[doctor] okay . and when was your last tetanus shot ?
[patient] i have no idea . probably high school .
[doctor] okay , we'll update that . what do you do for work ?
[patient] i'm a line cook .
[doctor] okay . so let me examine you . i'm going to keep your neck still . so you have a laceration on the top of your scalp , about three centimeters long . it's not deep , i do n't see any bone , and there's no debris or foreign body in it . i'm going to feel along the back of your neck . tell me where it hurts .
[patient] there , and there . kind of in the middle .
[doctor] okay . you have midline tenderness in the lower part of your neck , and you're tender in the muscles on both sides . now squeeze my fingers , push up , push down . good . your strength is five out of five in all four extremities . your sensation is normal and your reflexes are normal . your pupils are equal and reactive , and you're alert and answering everything appropriately .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] so because of how you hit your head and because you have midline tenderness , we got a ct scan of your neck and your head . hey dragon , show me the ct cervical spine . so looking at the ct of your neck , there is no fracture and no malalignment . the ct of your head shows no bleeding and no skull fracture .
[patient] okay , good .
[doctor] so for my assessment and plan . first , you have a cervical strain or sprain , which is an injury to the ligaments of the neck , from diving into the shallow end of the pool and striking the bottom . you were very lucky , because this is a classic way that people break their necks . the ct does not show a fracture . i'm going to clear the collar , but i'd like you to wear a soft collar for comfort for a few days only if you need it .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] for pain , ibuprofen six hundred milligrams every eight hours with food , and a muscle relaxer at night , cyclobenzaprine five milligrams . no driving on the muscle relaxer .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] second , the scalp laceration . we're going to clean it and close it with staples . those come out in seven to ten days . keep it dry for a day , and then you can wash your hair gently . we'll give you a tetanus booster today .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] i want you to follow up with your primary care doctor in one week , and if your neck pain is not better , we may get an mri . but if you get any numbness , tingling , weakness , trouble walking , or loss of bladder control , you need to come right back .
[patient] got it .
[doctor] and please , no diving into pools , especially if you do n't know the depth .
[patient] believe me , never again .
note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Neck pain and scalp laceration after a diving injury.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

{PATIENT_FIRST} {PATIENT_LAST} is a {AGE}-year-old male brought in by EMS with spinal motion restriction on {DATE_SPOKEN} after a diving injury at a public swimming pool. He was swimming and dove head first off the side into the shallow end, approximately 4 feet deep, striking the top of his head on the bottom of the pool. He reports a brief moment of seeing white but no loss of consciousness. He was assisted from the water and immobilized by the lifeguard. He reports immediate posterior neck pain, 5/10, radiating to the trapezius, and a mild headache at the laceration site. He denies numbness, tingling, weakness or electric shock sensations at any time. He denies nausea, vomiting, visual change or dyspnea. One alcoholic beverage 2 hours prior. No past medical history. No medications. Tetanus status unknown.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Line cook.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Neurological: Alert and oriented. Pupils equal and reactive. Strength 5/5 in all extremities. Sensation intact. Reflexes normal.
Head: 3 cm linear laceration of the vertex of the scalp, superficial, no foreign body, no exposed bone.
Neck: Lower cervical midline tenderness and bilateral paraspinal tenderness.

RESULTS

CT cervical spine: No fracture or malalignment.
CT head: No intracranial hemorrhage or skull fracture.

PROCEDURE

Scalp laceration irrigated and repaired with 4 staples. Tdap administered.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Cervical sprain, after diving into a swimming pool and striking the bottom.
- Medical Reasoning: Midline tenderness with normal CT and normal neurologic exam. Cervical collar cleared clinically.
- Medical Treatment: Soft collar for comfort as needed. Ibuprofen 600 mg every 8 hours with food. Cyclobenzaprine 5 mg at bedtime.
- Follow up with primary care in 1 week; MRI if persistent pain.

2. Laceration of the scalp without foreign body.
- Medical Treatment: Staple removal in 7 to 10 days. Wound care reviewed. Tetanus updated.

Return precautions reviewed for any numbness, weakness, gait change or bladder dysfunction.
